preamble: A lateral [l] becoming the nasal [n]. It occurs as a word-initial restriction in Sino-Korean (노인 noin 'old person' < 老人 ro-in), as coda adaptation of Pali/Sanskrit loans in Thai (kāla > กาล kaːn), and as the defining change of the 'n-dialects' of Cree-Innu (Proto-Algonquian *l > n).

examples.note: Initial-sound rule: word-initial liquid ㄹ becomes n before vowels other than i/y
Thai allows only nasal, glide or unreleased stop codas, so a final l is realized as n
